# Magic Box

> Browser and terminal tools for converting, decoding, generating and inspecting text.

- [Interactive tool list](https://mb.10oz.tw/list)
- [Usage and examples](https://github.com/XiaoXiaoSN/magic-box/blob/main/README.md)
- [Complete tool reference](https://github.com/XiaoXiaoSN/magic-box/blob/main/docs/tools.md)
- [Developer guide](https://github.com/XiaoXiaoSN/magic-box/blob/main/DEVELOPER.md)
- [Terminal UI](https://github.com/XiaoXiaoSN/magic-box/blob/main/docs/terminal-ui.md)

## Tools

### Color (color)

Convert HEX, RGB, and HSL colors; use ::cmyk, ::lighten, ::darken, or ::colormix for more formats and adjustments.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::cmyk, ::lighten, ::darken, ::colormix, ::mixcolor, ::blend.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
#ff6347
~~~~

### Color Contrast (color-contrast)

WCAG contrast ratio between two hex colors (space- or newline-separated).

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::contrast.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
#000000 #ffffff
::contrast
~~~~

### Escape String (escape-string)

Unescape JSON-escaped strings (\") and strip ANSI color codes.

Category: Decode. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: none.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
"{\"message\":\"something here\"}"
~~~~

### Base64 Decode (base64-decode)

Decode a Base64 encoded string back into readable text.

Category: Decode. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::language, ::lang, ::l.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
SGVsbG8gV29ybGQK
~~~~

### Cron Expression (cron-expression)

Translate cron expressions into human-readable schedules.

Category: Time. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::l, ::lang, ::locale.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
*/5 0 12 * * ?
~~~~

### Data Converter (data-converter)

Pretty-print and convert between JSON, YAML, TOML and XML.

Category: Format. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::json, ::tojson, ::yaml, ::yml, ::toyaml, ::toyml, ::toml, ::totoml, ::xml, ::toxml.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
{"name":"John Doe","age":30,"isStudent":false,"courses":[{"name":"History","credits":3},{"name":"Math","credits":4}]}

::toYAML
::toTOML
::toXML
~~~~

### JSON Tools (json-tools)

Merge, pick/omit, query (RFC 6901 JSON Pointer) and JSONL-convert JSON. ::jsonmerge (objects separated by a --- line), ::jsonpick=a,b, ::jsonomit=a,b, ::jsonpointer=/a/0, ::tojsonl, ::fromjsonl, ::jsonl (auto).

Category: Transform. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::jsonmerge, ::jsonpick, ::jsonomit, ::jsonpointer, ::tojsonl, ::fromjsonl, ::jsonl.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
{"a":1,"b":{"x":1}}
---
{"b":{"y":2},"c":3}
::jsonmerge
~~~~

### Date Calculate (date-calculate)

Add or subtract calendar or time units from a date, or compute the duration between two dates.

Category: Time. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::relative, ::timeago, ::timelater, ::relativetime.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
now + 7d
~~~~

### Duration (duration)

Convert numeric seconds/milliseconds or human duration formats (e.g. 10s, 8789sec, 1m48s, 1h3s) to/from human durations and clock formats.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::duration, ::humantime, ::parseduration, ::duration2s, ::humanize.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
3661
::duration
~~~~

### Generate QR Code (generate-qr-code)

Turn any input into a scannable QR code.

Category: Transform. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::qr, ::qrcode.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
https://mb.10oz.tw/list
::qrcode

~~~~

### Hash (hash)

Compute SHA hashes via Web Crypto and MD5 as a legacy checksum.

Category: Hash. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::hash, ::md5, ::sha1, ::sha256, ::sha384, ::sha512.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
hello world
::sha256
~~~~

### JWT Decode (jwt-decode)

Decode a JWT, render NumericDate claims in the preferred timezone, and optionally verify HS256/HS384/HS512 with ::secret.

Category: Decode. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::secret.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ.SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36POk6yJV_adQssw5c
~~~~

### ObjectId (objectid)

Decode a MongoDB ObjectId timestamp, random value, and counter with ::objectid.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::objectid, ::object-id.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
507f1f77bcf86cd799439011
::objectid
~~~~

### KSUID (ksuid)

Decode a KSUID timestamp and 128-bit payload with ::ksuid.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::ksuid.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
0ujtsYcgvSTl8PAuAdqWYSMnLOv
::ksuid
~~~~

### K8s Secret (k8s-secret)

Base64-decode all values inside a Kubernetes Secret YAML.

Category: Decode. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: none.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: mysecret
type: Opaque
data:
  username: dXNlcg==
  password: cGFzc3dvcmQ=
~~~~

### Math Expression (math-expression)

Evaluate mathematical expressions with standard operators.

Category: Compute. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::math.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
1 + 2 * (3 + 4) / 5
~~~~

### My IP (my-ip)

Show your public IP address along with geolocation.

Category: Info. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: none.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
ip
~~~~

### Now (now)

Display the current time in UTC, the preferred timezone, and Unix timestamp.

Category: Time. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: none.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
now
~~~~

### Password Generator (password-generator)

Generates a secure random password.

Category: Generate. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::password, ::pwd, ::pass, ::len, ::noupper, ::nolower, ::nonumbers, ::nosymbols.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
::password
~~~~

### Random Integer (random-integer)

Generate a random integer in a range of your choosing.

Category: Generate. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: none.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
random 1-6
~~~~

### Readable Bytes (readable-bytes)

Turn a comma-separated byte array into a readable string.

Category: Decode. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: none.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
83, 116, 114, 105, 110, 103, 32, 116, 111, 32, 66, 121, 116, 101, 115
~~~~

### Shorten URL (shorten-url)

Generate a short URL with an optional custom alias.

Category: Transform. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::surl, ::shorten.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
https://github.com/XiaoXiaoSN/magic-box
::surl

~~~~

### Time Format (time-format)

Convert an RFC 3339 timestamp into Unix seconds and milliseconds.

Category: Time. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: none.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
2025-06-21T19:34:57.530+08:00
~~~~

### URL Decode (url-decode)

Decode percent-encoded strings.

Category: Decode. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: none.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FXiaoXiaoSN%2Fmagic-box%3Ftab%3Dreadme
~~~~

### UUID (uuid)

Generate UUID v4 or v7 values, or inspect RFC 9562 version, variant, and embedded timestamps.

Category: Generate. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::uppercase, ::upper.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
uuid
~~~~

### Timestamp (timestamp)

Convert a Unix timestamp back to a human-readable date.

Category: Time. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::timestamp, ::unix, ::ts.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
1735794245
~~~~

### Base64 Encode (base64-encode)

Encode a string to Base64.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: none.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
Hello World
~~~~

### Word Wrap (word-wrap)

Wrap text to a column width at word boundaries. Use ::wrap=N for width N (default 80).

Category: Transform. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::wrap, ::wordwrap.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
::wrap=20
~~~~

### A1Z26 (a1z26)

Encode letters to their position numbers (A=1..Z=26) or decode numbers back to letters.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::a1z26, ::a1z26encode, ::a1z26decode.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
hello
::a1z26
~~~~

### ASCII Code (ascii-code)

Look up a character or a code point: decimal, hex, octal, binary, and the glyph.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::ascii, ::charcode.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
A
::ascii
~~~~

### Aspect Ratio (aspect-ratio)

Simplify width x height into an aspect ratio (e.g. 1920x1080 → 16:9).

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::ratio, ::aspect.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
1920x1080
::ratio
~~~~

### Base32 (base32)

RFC 4648 Base32 encode/decode. ::base32 to encode, ::base32decode to decode.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::base32, ::base32encode, ::base32decode.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
hello
::base32
~~~~

### Base58 (base58)

Encode text to Base58 (Bitcoin alphabet) or decode Base58 back to text.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::base58, ::base58encode, ::base58decode.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
Hello World!
::base58
~~~~

### Base62 (base62)

Encode a non-negative integer to Base62, or decode a Base62 string to a number.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::base62, ::base62encode, ::base62decode.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
123456789
::base62
~~~~

### Base85 (base85)

Encode text to Ascii85 (Base85) or decode Ascii85 back to text.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::base85, ::base85encode, ::base85decode, ::ascii85.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
hello
::base85
~~~~

### basE91 (base91)

Encode text to basE91 or decode a basE91 string.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::base91, ::base91encode, ::base91decode.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
hello
::base91
~~~~

### Text to Binary (text-to-binary)

Convert text to space-separated 8-bit binary (UTF-8), or binary back to text.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::binary, ::tobinary, ::binarydecode, ::frombinary.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
Hi
::binary
~~~~

### BMI (bmi)

Compute Body Mass Index. Input: "<weight>kg <height>m" or "<weight>lb <height>in".

Category: Calculate. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::bmi.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
70kg 1.75m
::bmi
~~~~

### Dice Roll (dice-roll)

Roll six-sided dice. Specify a count from 1 to 20; defaults to 1. ::roll or ::dice=3.

Category: Generate. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::roll, ::dice.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
::roll
~~~~

### Easter (easter)

Compute the date of Easter Sunday (Gregorian) and Lunar New Year for a given year.

Category: Calculate. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::easter, ::lny, ::cny, ::lunarnewyear.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
2025
::easter
~~~~

### Fraction (fraction)

Convert a decimal to a simplified fraction, or a fraction (a/b) to a decimal.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::fraction, ::tofraction.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
0.75
::fraction
~~~~

### Frequency (frequency)

Count character frequencies in the input, sorted by count.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::freq, ::frequency.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
hello world
::freq
~~~~

### GCD / LCM (gcd-lcm)

Compute the GCD and LCM of a list of integers (comma or space separated).

Category: Calculate. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::gcd, ::lcm.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
12, 18, 24
::gcd
~~~~

### Distance (distance)

Great-circle distance between two coordinates. Input: "lat1,lng1 to lat2,lng2".

Category: Calculate. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::haversine, ::distance.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
40.7128,-74.0060 to 51.5074,-0.1278
::haversine
~~~~

### Line Tools (line-tools)

De-duplicate or reverse the lines of a text block.

Category: Transform. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::uniquelines, ::reverselines.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
banana
apple
cherry
apple
::uniquelines
~~~~

### Power Convert (power-convert)

Convert power between W, kW, mW, MW, hp, PS, BTU/h.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::power.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
100 hp
::power
~~~~

### Semver (semver)

Parse and validate a Semantic Version string into its components.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::semver.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
1.2.3-beta.1+build.5
::semver
~~~~

### Snowflake (snowflake)

Parse a Snowflake ID (Discord/Twitter) into its timestamp and components.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::snowflake, ::epoch.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
175928847299117063
::snowflake
~~~~

### Sort Lines (sort-lines)

Sort the lines of text. ::sortlines (asc), modifiers ::desc, ::numeric, ::unique, ::ci (case-insensitive).

Category: Transform. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::sortlines, ::sort, ::numeric, ::ci, ::caseinsensitive, ::desc, ::reverse, ::unique, ::uniq.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
banana
apple
cherry
::sortlines
~~~~

### Soundex (soundex)

Compute the American Soundex phonetic code for each word in the input.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::soundex.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
Robert
::soundex
~~~~

### Speed Convert (speed-convert)

Convert a speed between m/s, km/h, mph, knots, and ft/s.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::speed.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
100 km/h
::speed
~~~~

### Subnet (subnet)

Calculate IPv4 CIDR or IP/netmask subnets, split a network, and test membership with ::subnet.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::subnet, ::cidr, ::split, ::contains.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
192.168.1.10/24
::subnet
~~~~

### Temperature (temperature)

Convert a temperature between Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin. e.g. "100C ::temp".

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::temp, ::temperature.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
100C
::temp
~~~~

### Text Diff (text-diff)

Paste a second text with ::diff, or separate two texts with --- and use ::textdiff.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::diff, ::textdiff, ::linediff, ::lang, ::language, ::l.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
foo
bar
---
foo
baz
::textdiff
~~~~

### Text Reverse (text-reverse)

Reverse the characters of the input string without splitting grapheme clusters.

Category: Transform. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::reverse, ::reversetext.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
hello 😀
::reverse
~~~~

### Two's Complement (twos-complement)

Show the two's-complement binary/hex of an integer at a bit width. ::twos=<bits> (default 8).

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::twos, ::twoscomplement.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
-42
::twos=8
~~~~

### ULID (ulid)

Generate a ULID (::ulid) or decode the timestamp of an existing ULID (::ulid=<ulid> or ::ulidparse).

Category: Generate. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::ulid, ::ulidparse.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
::ulid
~~~~

### Unicode Normalize (unicode-normalize)

Normalize text to a Unicode form (NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD). ::normalize=nfc (default NFC).

Category: Transform. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::normalize, ::unicodenormalize.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
café
::normalize=nfd
~~~~

### Unit Converter (unit-converter)

Convert units automatically for length, area, volume, mass, temperature, speed, pressure, power, energy, data size, data rate, and time (e.g. 100 km, 50 MB to GB, 37 C).

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::unit, ::convert.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
100 km to mi
~~~~

### Week Number (week-number)

Compute the ISO 8601 week number (and weekday, day-of-year) for a date.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::weeknum, ::isoweek.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
2024-01-01
::weeknum
~~~~

### Whitespace Clean (whitespace-clean)

Trim each line, collapse internal whitespace runs, and remove blank lines.

Category: Transform. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::clean, ::cleanws.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
  hello   world  


  foo  bar
::clean
~~~~

### Words to Number (words-to-number)

Parse English number words into an integer (e.g. "one thousand two hundred" → 1200).

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::wordstonum, ::wordstonumber.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
one million two hundred thirty-four thousand
::wordstonum
~~~~

### Zodiac Sign (zodiac-sign)

Determine the Western zodiac sign for a date (MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD).

Category: Calculate. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::zodiac, ::starsign.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
03-21
::zodiac
~~~~

### Word Count (word-count)

Count the lines, words and characters in any input.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: none.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
There are so many sounds in the world.
i'mdifficult

~~~~

### Markdown TOC (markdown-toc)

Generate a table of contents (nested bullet list with anchor links) from Markdown headings.

Category: Transform. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::toc, ::tableofcontents.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
# Title
## Section A
### Sub
## Section B
::toc
~~~~

### Punycode (punycode)

Convert an internationalized domain name to/from its Punycode (xn--) ASCII form.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::punycode, ::punycodeencode, ::idn, ::punycodedecode, ::idndecode.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
münchen.de
::punycode
~~~~

### Radix Convert (radix-convert)

Convert an integer between arbitrary bases (2-36). e.g. ::radix=16:2 for hex→binary.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::radix, ::baseconvert.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
ff
::radix=16:2
~~~~

### Query String (query-string)

Convert a URL query string to JSON, or a flat JSON object to a query string.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::qs, ::querystring.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
a=1&b=2&b=3
::qs
~~~~

### Hex Dump (hex-dump)

Produce a canonical hex + ASCII dump of the input (like hexdump -C).

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::hexdump, ::xxd.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
Hello, World!
::hexdump
~~~~

### Text to Hex (text-to-hex)

Convert text to a hex string (UTF-8) or decode a hex string back to text.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::hex, ::tohex, ::hexdecode, ::fromhex.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
Hi
::hex
~~~~

### URL Parse (url-parse)

Break a URL into protocol, host, port, path, query, and hash.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::urlparse, ::parseurl.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
https://user:pass@example.com:8080/a/b?x=1&y=2#frag
::urlparse
~~~~

### Readable Text Color (readable-text-color)

Given a background hex color, pick the readable foreground (black or white) and the WCAG contrast.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::oncolor, ::textcolor.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
#3498db
::oncolor
~~~~

### Credit Card Info (credit-card-info)

Detect the card brand from a number and check Luhn validity (masks the number).

Category: Validate. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::cardtype, ::creditcard, ::cardinfo.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
4111111111111111
::cardinfo
~~~~

### Glob to Regex (glob-to-regex)

Convert a shell glob pattern (*, ?, [...], **) into an anchored regular expression.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::glob2regex, ::globregex.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
src/**/*.ts
::glob2regex
~~~~

### HSV (hsv)

Convert a color between hex/RGB and HSV (HSB).

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::hsv, ::hsb.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
#ff6347
::hsv
~~~~

### IPv6 (ipv6)

Expand and compress an IPv6 address (RFC 5952).

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::ipv6.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
2001:db8::1
::ipv6
~~~~

### IEEE 754 (ieee-754)

Show the IEEE-754 (double + single) bit representation of a number, or decode a hex pattern back to a float.

Category: Analyze. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::ieee754, ::floatbits.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
3.14
::ieee754
~~~~

### MAC Address (mac-address)

Normalize a MAC address and show its formats, OUI prefix, and flags.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::mac, ::macaddress.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
01:23:45:67:89:ab
::mac
~~~~

### Morse Code (morse-code)

Encode text to Morse code or decode Morse code back to text.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::morse, ::morseencode, ::morsedecode.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
SOS
::morse
~~~~

### Port Lookup (port-lookup)

Look up a well-known port number or service name. ::port

Category: Decode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::port, ::portlookup.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
443
::port
~~~~

### Unicode Escape (unicode-escape)

Escape text to \uXXXX sequences, or unescape \uXXXX / \u{...} back to text.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::unicodeescape, ::uescape, ::unicodeunescape, ::uunescape.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
héllo 😀
::unicodeescape
~~~~

### HMAC (hmac)

Compute HMAC of the input with a key: ::hmac=<key>. Select algorithms with ::sha256, ::sha1, ::sha512 (default: all); each also accepts the key, e.g. ::sha512=<key>.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::hmac, ::hmacsha1, ::hmacsha256, ::hmacsha512, ::sha1, ::sha256, ::sha512.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
::hmac=key
~~~~

### PBKDF2 (pbkdf2)

Derive a key from the input password: ::pbkdf2=<salt>. Options ::iterations=<n>, ::dklen=<bytes>, and the PRF via ::prf=sha256|sha1|sha512 or bare ::sha256/::sha1/::sha512 (default HMAC-SHA256).

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::pbkdf2, ::prf, ::iterations, ::dklen, ::sha1, ::sha256, ::sha512.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
password
::pbkdf2=salt
~~~~

### Local AI (local-ai)

Run a small language model entirely in this browser with WebGPU: ask, translate, rewrite or summarize. Nothing is downloaded or generated until you ask for it, and prompts never leave the device. ::ai

Category: Generate. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::ai, ::localai.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
::ai
~~~~

### CRC-32 (crc-32)

Compute the CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3) checksum of the input text.

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::crc32.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
hello
::crc32
~~~~

### Crockford Base32 (crockford-base32)

Encode text to Crockford's Base32 or decode it back (case-insensitive, no padding).

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::crockford, ::crockfordencode, ::crockforddecode.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
hello
::crockford
~~~~

### Case Converter (case-converter)

Convert each line between camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, CONSTANT_CASE, kebab-case, Title Case, dot.case, path/case, Sentence case, lowercase and UPPERCASE. Use ::case to list formats or ::case=<format> to select one.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::case, ::camel, ::camelcase, ::pascal, ::pascalcase, ::snake, ::snakecase, ::kebab, ::kebabcase, ::constant, ::constantcase, ::dot, ::dotcase, ::path, ::pathcase, ::title, ::titlecase, ::sentence, ::sentencecase, ::lower, ::lowercase, ::upper, ::uppercase.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
XMLHttpRequest userID v2ApiKey
::case
~~~~

### Certificate Decode (certificate-decode)

Decode PEM X.509 certificates and CA bundles locally. ::cert

Category: Decode. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::cert, ::certificate, ::ca.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
Paste a PEM certificate here
::cert
~~~~

### Cheat Sheet (cheat-sheet)

Offline command examples. Enter curl, cheat:git, or ::cheat=jq.

Category: Reference. Enabled by default on the web: true.
Option keys: ::cheat, ::cheatsheet.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
curl
~~~~

### Coordinates (coordinates)

Convert a coordinate between decimal degrees, DDM, DMS, Plus Code, Geohash, UTM, MGRS and geo URI. ::coord shows every format; ::dms, ::pluscode, ::geohash, ::utm, … show just that one. Accepts lat/lng in any of the angle formats, a full Plus Code or a Geohash.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::coord, ::coords, ::latlng, ::latlon, ::dd, ::decimal, ::ddm, ::dms, ::pluscode, ::olc, ::geohash, ::utm, ::mgrs, ::geo, ::geouri.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
40.446195, -79.948862
::coord
~~~~

### HTML Entities (html-entities)

Decode HTML5 character references without parsing markup, or encode text with ::htmlencode (add =all to encode non-ASCII characters).

Category: Encode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::htmlencode, ::htmldecode.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
&amp;lt; &#x1F600;
::htmldecode
~~~~

### HTTP Status (http-status)

Look up an IANA-assigned HTTP status by code or exact reason phrase with ::http, http 502, or status 404.

Category: Decode. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::http.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
404
::http
~~~~

### chmod Calculator (chmod-calculator)

Convert absolute octal, rwx symbolic, and u/g/o permission modes with ::chmod. Use ::umask=022 for standard new-file and directory permissions.

Category: Convert. Enabled by default on the web: false.
Option keys: ::chmod, ::umask.

Example (each ::option starts a new line):
~~~~text
4755
::chmod
~~~~
